items.what: Listed Alaska as a toss up Senate race where Democrats lead by 3, and warned Democrats to trust no one as GOP has beaten polls in Trump states.
Said the Ohio governor race has flipped to Amy Acton, up 4, and called Ramaswamy's standing with independents the worst this century.
Named Ohio among six toss up Senate races and warned Democrats of a big siren because polls are within the margin of error.
Named Michigan among six toss up Senate races Democrats need to win at least three of.
Named Iowa among six toss up Senate races in his big siren segment.
Named Kansas among toss up Senate races, with polling showing a tie or Democrats up a few points.
Broke down unusual Democratic strength in Texas beyond Talarico, citing a 20 point shift on the statewide House ballot and a big Hispanic swing.
Said a Talarico win would give Democrats a 78% chance of winning the Senate and showed Talarico with a 70% chance to win Texas.
In a YouTube forecast video listed Maine as a Democratic lead of 3 points on the path to a Democratic sweep.
In a YouTube forecast video listed Ohio as a Democratic lead of 3 points.
Highlighted Jon Ossoff leading by 13 points as one of three Southern Senate races where Democrats lead.
Highlighted Roy Cooper leading by 9 points in North Carolina, which has not elected a Democratic senator since 2008.
Highlighted James Talarico leading by 2 points in Texas, calling it a possibly historic year for Democrats in the South.
Said North Carolina, with Democrats up 7, was the only Senate seat Democrats could count on, arguing the math was not there for a majority.
Called the Collins vs Platner race a contest with no clear leader in his Senate math segment.
Said Talarico would win if the election were held now and Paxton loses if he will not debate.
Said he worries about Alaska for Dan Sullivan.
Predicted Republican Ashley Hinson will win.
Said Democrats will fall short in Kansas but it is a race.
Predicted Susan Collins will win.
Called Michigan close with Mike Rogers having a good shot.
Said he believes in Republican Michele Tafoya but would not predict a win.
Predicted Pete Ricketts will win and called Dan Osborn a phony.
Agreed Democrats will flip the North Carolina seat.
Said he is worried for Republicans in Ohio.
Called South Carolina a hope for Democrats but not real.
On Fox News Radio said Trump expects Paxton to lose and is looking for someone to blame, adding I really don't care.
On the Journal Editorial Report said Democrats got the better candidate in Josh Turek, though Hinson is strong.
On the Journal Editorial Report called Sherrod Brown a terrific candidate and predicted a horserace with Jon Husted.
Called Maine the Senate tipping point state, with Troy Jackson narrowly ahead of Susan Collins in his polling error test.
His Silver Bulletin forecast gave James Talarico a 74.3% chance to beat Ken Paxton.
His Silver Bulletin forecast gave Roy Cooper a 95.3% chance to beat Michael Whatley.
His Silver Bulletin forecast gave Sherrod Brown a 73.9% chance to unseat Jon Husted.
His polling average showed Mary Peltola slightly ahead of Dan Sullivan, 48.1% to 46.6%.
His FLIPR forecast rated Texas Lean D with a 63% chance of a Talarico pickup.
His forecast gave Roy Cooper a 90% chance of defeating Michael Whatley.
His forecast gave Troy Jackson a 69% chance of defeating Susan Collins.
Pushed back on an El-Sayed supporter's rosy reading of his primary win.
Dismissed an internal Platner poll released amid his sexting scandal.
Fox News Power Rankings moved North Carolina from Lean D to Likely D.
Fox News Power Rankings moved South Carolina Senate from Solid R to Likely R.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Florida governor from Solid R to Likely R.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Vermont governor from Solid R to Likely R.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Oregon governor from Likely D to Lean D, citing Gov. Kotek's lethargic debate.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Georgia Senate from Lean D to Likely D.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Kansas Senate from Likely R to Lean R.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Abbott vs Hinojosa from Likely R to Lean R.
Fox News Power Rankings moved Alaska governor from Lean R to Toss-Up.
Fox News Power Rankings moved FL-25 toward Democrats among seven Florida House shifts.
Called Texas a coin flip, praised Talarico and called Paxton perhaps the worst candidate in the country.
Called Alaska a coin flip, noting Mary Peltola led the first round.
Said Ossoff is the least likely competitive incumbent to lose.
Called the Iowa Senate race a coin flip.
Said Maine is in play and will be close but Collins is a survivor.
Predicted El-Sayed will win and hold the seat.
Agreed Democrats will flip North Carolina.
Said Sherrod Brown should win, though he could be painted as establishment.
On The Arena said El-Sayed should answer quickly and pivot to the economy, calling his I am smarter than you posture not appealing.
Said Talarico knows his real views are very unpopular with Texans as he distances himself from past rhetoric.
Ran a segment on El-Sayed's campaign and the GOP strategy in Michigan under the line that the only poll that matters is on Election Day.
Said Texas would dance into 'economic Armageddon' with Talarico as senator over his past comments on capitalism and oil and gas.
Attacked Democratic nominee Dr. Annie Andrews ahead of the Republican Senate runoff, saying under the white coat is a left wing agenda.
Called Abdul El-Sayed 'weird' and obsessed with sex over his comments about JD Vance's children and mocked his posture.
Called DSA member Angie Nixon's Democratic Senate primary win the best midterm news for the GOP since Platner.
Mocked the Maine Democratic Senate debate and its candidates' policies and discussed the effect on Susan Collins.
Ran a segment on a report about Democratic candidate Graham Platner's alleged past behavior and relationships.

items.what: Interviewed Ohio Senate candidate Sherrod Brown; the episode page listed it as 5 days old on Oct 22.
Interviewed Democratic Senate candidate Annie Andrews.
Interviewed Democratic governor candidate Aaron Ford.
Interviewed independent Senate candidate Dan Osborn.
Interviewed Bob Brooks, billed as the Democratic nominee in the most flippable district in Pennsylvania.
Interviewed Xavier Becerra, whom the episode called the future governor of California.
Hosted a 2WAY panel where Hans Nichols and Eliana Johnson named Alaska, Texas and Ohio as the Senate seats most likely to flip.
His 2WAY 'Midterm Blitz' coverage described both the Texas governor and Senate races as in play, citing Vance's return to the state and money flowing to Paxton.
His 2WAY coverage focused on Republican Rick Jackson's absence from a Georgia governor debate and candidates dodging debates.
Told Megyn Kelly that if the election were held today James Talarico would beat Ken Paxton unless Republicans change the race's trajectory.
Ran a Morning Meeting segment on Maine's evolving Democratic Senate field and the deadline for Graham Platner to exit the race.
Ran a segment on conservative influencers and Elon Musk spreading the false Ohio mental facility claim about Talarico.
Covered the Detroit Free Press note refusing pro Rogers letters over racist attacks on El-Sayed.
Covered Trump attacking Talarico and criticizing Paxton's speech and appearance at the GOP midterm convention.
Covered Paxton pleading with donors after Talarico built a large fundraising lead.
Contrasted Republican reaction to the Platner allegations with GOP silence on allegations against Trump.
On her AM Update she amplified debunked claims that James Talarico was treated at an Ohio mental health facility during his absence from the trail.
Argued El-Sayed is doing well because of his hard line on Israel and domestic focus, and called Republican Mike Rogers a 'neocon' whose attacks will not energize the GOP base.
Hosted Mark Halperin and called his view that Talarico is on track to beat Paxton 'stunning', noting polls show Talarico ahead.
Ripped Senate primary candidate Haley Stevens' accent and called her a new Jasmine Crockett.
Told Mediaite that Jen Kiggans's 2nd District is a key early election night bellwether.
Flagged Tom Perriello's challenge to John McGuire in the 5th District as a long shot Democratic target worth watching.
Said he is skeptical the Sununu versus Pappas Senate race is truly competitive.
Said Democrats might win three of the five South Texas seats Republicans drew to target Hispanic voters.
On Today warned a tide seems to be working against Democrats in Minnesota's Flanagan vs Tafoya race.
At a Princeton talk he called Susan Collins's seat the most obvious Democratic Senate opportunity.
